ABSTRACT

India’s construction industry employs over 74 million unorganized daily-wage workers, representing the second-largest employer in the national economy. Despite rapid digitization across commercial infrastructure, construction sites continue to rely almost exclusively on manual, handwritten paper registers (“muster rolls”) maintained by site supervisors and petty subcontractors (“maistries”). This legacy system is severely broken: over 68% of daily-wage laborers report weekly wage disputes, losing an average of ₹1,150 to ₹1,400 monthly due to undocumented hour cuts, misplaced tea advances, and arbitrary attendance deductions. Concurrently, general contractors and developers suffer from an estimated 10% to 14% payroll leakage caused by ghost workers, proxy check-ins, and fabricated headcounts. While biometric fingerprint scanners have been attempted on tier-1 sites, they fail catastrophically in practice—demonstrating an 84.2% optical failure rate because abrasive cement dust, lime slurry, wet mortar, and heavy handling wear down workers’ epidermal ridges. Furthermore, 71.8% of daily-wage laborers own basic 2G keypad phones without touchscreen or mobile data capabilities, rendering modern smartphone-first attendance applications exclusionary and ineffective.

To resolve this multi-faceted socio-technical crisis, BuildEase was conceived and developed following a rigorous 5-stage Design Thinking methodology (Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, and Test). Grounded in direct ethnographic field interviews with site masons (such as 42-year-old Senior Mason Murugesan K. in Tiruppur) and site civil foremen, BuildEase reframes workforce management from a top-down surveillance mechanism into a transparent, inclusive, dual-sided ledger of trust. The proposed platform integrates three resilient architectural layers: (1) an edge AI biometric tablet kiosk utilizing lightweight YuNet face detection and SFace neural feature extraction running entirely client-side in under 3 seconds per worker, impervious to dust-covered hands; (2) a telecom-integrated 2G GSM Interactive Voice Response (IVR) missed-call gateway with daily rotating gate PINs, enabling workers with basic keypad feature phones to independently verify check-ins without internet connectivity; and (3) an offline-first Progressive Web Application (PWA) powered by IndexedDB with background optimistic sync, guaranteeing 100% operational uptime in cellular dead zones such as basement excavations and reinforced concrete towers.

Crucially, BuildEase embeds human-centric fail-safes: optical recognition failures triggered by direct sunlight or medical bandages never automatically deduct wages; instead, shifts are preserved in a supervisor “Pending Review” queue. The automated payroll calculation engine transparently enforces the statutory wage formula [Wage = (Rate × Verified Hours) − Advances], producing instant multi-lingual SMS receipts in 5 regional languages (Hindi, Tamil, Marathi, Bengali, and Assamese) and 1-click NPCI NACH/NEFT automated disbursement batches. BuildEase aligns directly with United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth, SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure, and SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities), restoring fundamental dignity, trust, and fiscal accuracy to the construction ecosystem.

CHAPTER 1
INTRODUCTION

1.1 Introduction

The construction sector forms the backbone of global physical infrastructure development and serves as the second-largest employer in developing economies such as India, engaging more than 74 million daily-wage laborers, masons, carpenters, bar-benders, and unskilled helpers. Despite the monumental scale and capital intensity of contemporary civil engineering projects, human capital management on ground-level jobsites remains trapped in archaic, manual practices established over a century ago. On the overwhelming majority of construction sites across urban and peri-urban India, workforce tracking and wage administration are conducted entirely through handwritten paper registers, colloquially known as “muster rolls,” maintained by field supervisors and petty labour contractors (“maistries”).

This reliance on paper-based record keeping introduces severe structural inefficiencies, pervasive financial leakage, and endemic labor friction. Daily-wage laborers operate in physically punishing conditions characterized by airborne abrasive cement dust, wet mortar, heavy aggregate handling, and extreme weather exposure. At the conclusion of a 6-day workweek, workers must undergo a protracted, non-transparent reconciliation process where supervisors manually tally shifts, deduct arbitrary amounts for mid-week tea and meal advances, and impose unverified late penalties. Because workers possess no tangible or immutable documentation of their daily hours, disputes are frequent and heated. Empirical studies indicate that more than 68% of construction laborers suffer from regular wage shortfalls, forfeiting between ₹1,000 and ₹1,500 every month—a substantial portion of their living income.

Simultaneously, general contractors and project developers face crippling operational and financial challenges under the legacy system. The lack of verifiable, real-time site verification enables widespread fraud, including the billing of “ghost workers” (individuals listed on muster rolls who were never physically present), buddy punching, and inflated labor rosters. Industry audits suggest that project developers experience 10% to 14% unauthorized payroll leakage on commercial sites. Attempts to deploy commercial enterprise biometric hardware (such as optical fingerprint scanners) have failed dramatically due to the abrasive erosion of workers’ epidermal ridges caused by caustic cement compounds, yielding field rejection rates upwards of 80%. Furthermore, standard modern attendance software requires individual smartphones and high-speed mobile data connections—technological luxuries absent among the 70%+ of the workforce who carry basic 2G keypad feature phones.

BuildEase emerges as an empathetic, socio-technically grounded intervention engineered specifically to dismantle these systemic bottlenecks. By reframing workforce management as an instrument of mutual transparency rather than top-down surveillance, BuildEase delivers a resilient multi-modal ecosystem combining edge-computed facial biometrics, inclusive 2G GSM cellular voice channels, offline-first data replication, and mathematical payroll automation.

1.2 Objective

The primary objective of the BuildEase project is to design, develop, and empirically validate an equitable, transparent, and resilient workforce management and payroll platform tailored specifically to the operational constraints of construction sites. The specific sub-objectives are delineated below:

  • Eliminate Biometric Rejection on Abrasive Hands: Implement an edge-based, contactless facial recognition pipeline utilizing lightweight neural architectures (YuNet and SFace) that authenticates workers in under 3 seconds per entry, entirely eliminating dependence on damaged epidermal ridges.
  • Provide 100% Inclusive Access for 2G Keypad Users: Integrate a telecom-backed Interactive Voice Response (IVR) and missed-call telephony gateway featuring rotating gate PINs, enabling non-smartphone users to independently log and verify site attendance without mobile data.
  • Guarantee Continuous Offline-First Operation: Architect a robust client-side caching and synchronization engine utilizing IndexedDB, ensuring zero operational downtime in deep basements, elevator shafts, and remote peripheral sites lacking cellular connectivity.
  • Automate Transparent, Dispute-Free Wage Calculations: Enforce an immutable mathematical payroll engine based on the statutory formula Wage = (Daily Rate × Verified Shifts) − Documented Advances, coupled with automated multi-lingual SMS wage receipts and 1-click bank transfer batch generation.
  • Eradicate Ghost Workers and Payroll Fraud: Couple GPS geofencing verification (100-meter radius) with rapid digital foreman muster sign-off workflows to eliminate fabricated headcounts and unauthorized labor inflation.
  • Align with Global Sustainable Development Goals: Promote United Nations SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure), and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) by safeguarding worker wage entitlements and human dignity.

1.3 Scope

The operational and technical scope of BuildEase encompasses all critical touchpoints across the daily shift lifecycle on small, medium, and mega construction projects:

  • Target Workforce: Daily-wage laborers, skilled artisans (masons, carpenters, bar-benders, plumbers, electricians), apprentice helpers, and interstate migrant workers across diverse linguistic backgrounds.
  • Hardware Deployment: Low-cost, ruggedized IP65 Android gate tablet kiosks for high-throughput facial capture, standard supervisor mobile tablets/smartphones for muster sign-offs, and ordinary 2G GSM cellular handsets.
  • Software Environment: Modern browser-compatible Progressive Web Application (PWA) operating on React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Node.js/Express REST microservices, client-side ONNX Runtime Web, and IndexedDB persistent storage.
  • Administrative & Compliance Domain: Shift scheduling, skill categorization, trade task allocation, daily site reports (DSR), advance payment tracking, automated muster roll generation, audit-ready CSV exports for BOCW (Building and Other Construction Workers) Welfare Board regulatory compliance, and multi-lingual worker SMS communication.

CHAPTER 2
PROBLEM DEFINITION

2.1 Existing System

In the contemporary construction ecosystem, workforce tracking is predominantly executed via two legacy modalities:

  1. Manual Paper-Based Muster Rolls: Site supervisors or labour contractors manually record names, morning arrival marks, and evening departure marks in paper notebooks. At mid-day, cash advances for tea, lunch, or emergency expenses are scribbled in margins or separate informal chits. At the close of the week, the supervisor attempts to mentally reconcile hours worked, advance deductions, and overtime adjustments. This modality is fraught with severe vulnerabilities:
    • Paper records are susceptible to physical damage, cement water contamination, ink smudging, and deliberate post-facto alterations.
    • Supervisors spend 1.5 to 2.5 hours every evening transcribing, verifying, and computing headcounts, pulling critical technical personnel away from active site safety supervision.
    • Workers have zero visibility into what has been written; their wages are subject to unilateral deductions without documented proof or recourse.
  2. Traditional Optical Biometric Hardware (Fingerprint Scanners): On select large-scale infrastructure projects, developers have attempted to introduce wall-mounted biometric fingerprint attendance terminals. In site reality, these systems fail catastrophically:
    • Construction materials—specifically Portland cement, hydrated lime, coarse sand, and abrasive gravel—rapidly erode the papillary friction ridges of workers’ fingers.
    • Dust, oil, slurry, and wet skin create extreme optical diffusion on glass scanner platen surfaces, generating false rejection rates (FRR) in excess of 80%.
    • Prolonged scanner queues at dawn cause severe bottlenecking, leading supervisors to abandon the machines and revert back to manual registers.

2.2 Problem Statement

Construction sites are plagued by an adversarial, non-transparent labor paradigm where daily-wage workers lose substantial portions of their entitled earnings to paper-record tampering, unrecorded advance deductions, and optical biometric failures, while developers and contractors suffer massive payroll losses (10–14%) to ghost workers and fabricated headcounts. The fundamental challenge is to engineer an inclusive, zero-fraud, offline-resilient workforce ecosystem that operates seamlessly without requiring smartphones from laborers, authenticates workers regardless of damaged hands, guarantees instant dispute-free mathematical wage payouts, and restores dignity and trust to the construction site.

2.3 Constraints

The development and deployment of BuildEase are bounded by rigorous real-world field constraints:

  • Physical & Environmental Constraints: Extreme outdoor ambient temperatures (10°C to 45°C), heavy direct solar glare, intense airborne abrasive cement dust, wet concrete slurry, and erratic grid electrical supply.
  • Connectivity Constraints: Deep subterranean basements (3 levels underground), reinforced concrete shear walls, and remote peri-urban greenfield locations where cellular 4G/5G signals drop to zero bars.
  • Device & User Constraints: Over 70% of laborers do not possess smartphones, cannot read English text, and possess low digital literacy; interactive solutions must not demand complex app installations or touchscreen interactions from workers.
  • Throughput & Timing Constraints: Site entry gates experience sharp rushes where 150 to 300 workers arrive between 07:15 AM and 07:35 AM; verification per individual must execute in under 3 seconds to prevent gate congestion.
  • Cost Constraints: System hardware must utilize accessible, off-the-shelf Android tablets rather than prohibitively expensive proprietary industrial biometric terminals.

2.4 People Affected

The breakdown of manual workforce management directly damages several key demographic groups:

  • Daily-Wage Laborers & Artisans (Primary Victims): Suffer immediate financial hardship from unrecorded hours and arbitrary wage cuts, experiencing severe emotional humiliation, anxiety, and distrust toward site authorities.
  • Interstate Migrant Workers: Laborers migrating from eastern or northern India (speaking Hindi, Bengali, or Assamese) working on southern sites face acute linguistic isolation, making them especially vulnerable to exploitative subcontractor deductions.
  • Site Civil Supervisors & Foremen: Endure daily burnout, spending hours cross-verifying registers, handling volatile Saturday pay disputes, and risking personal liability for headcount discrepancies.
  • General Contractors & Developers: Incur substantial unrecoverable financial overhead from ghost-worker invoices, project schedule delays resulting from labor walkouts, and exposure to statutory BOCW labor audit penalties.

2.5 Design Challenge

Following design thinking inquiry, the overarching design challenge was formulated into seven core “How Might We” (HMW) questions:

  1. HMW-1 (Biometric Inclusion): How might we accurately authenticate daily-wage workers in under 3 seconds without relying on damaged or dust-coated fingertips?
  2. HMW-2 (Device Accessibility): How might we empower workers who only possess basic 2G keypad feature phones to independently log attendance and verify wage records without internet access?
  3. HMW-3 (Offline Resilience): How might we maintain complete, uninterrupted verification and muster functionality on construction sites with zero cellular or network connectivity?
  4. HMW-4 (Wage Transparency): How might we eliminate end-of-month wage disputes by mathematically linking verified shift hours and mid-day advances directly to automated multi-lingual pay receipts?
  5. HMW-5 (Fraud Prevention): How might we eradicate ghost-worker billing and proxy check-ins without imposing humiliating or time-consuming security checkpoints on laborers?
  6. HMW-6 (Human-Centric Fail-Safe): How might we ensure that edge algorithm false rejections or lighting glitches never result in automatic wage forfeiture or worker penalties?
  7. HMW-7 (Operational Efficiency): How might we compress the supervisor’s evening muster reconciliation workflow from 2 hours of manual ledger tallying down to under 15 minutes of digital sign-off?

3.3 Software Description

3.3.1 Edge AI Biometric Subsystem (YuNet + SFace)

Rather than streaming uncompressed video frames to remote cloud servers (which inevitably induces latency and fails in cellular dead zones), BuildEase utilizes client-side ONNX Runtime Web. The gate kiosk webcam stream feeds into YuNet, an ultra-compact convolutional neural network optimized for real-time edge face detection. Detected bounding boxes are aligned using 5 facial landmarks and passed to SFace, an 8-layer deep feature extraction network that outputs a compact 128-dimensional floating-point embedding vector. Cosine similarity matching is executed locally against pre-cached site workforce templates in under 300 milliseconds.

3.3.2 2G GSM IVR & PIN Telephony Subsystem

To bridge the digital divide for workers lacking smartphones, BuildEase implements a carrier-grade telephony gateway. When a worker arrives at the gate, they place a toll-free missed call to the project’s dedicated 1800-number. The system answers via an automated voice prompt in the worker’s preferred language (e.g., Tamil or Hindi) and prompts them to enter the daily 4-digit “Gate PIN” written on the physical muster board. Upon entry, the system verifies caller-ID against the site roster and logs the check-in event, returning an automated SMS confirmation.

3.3.3 Offline-First IndexedDB Replication Engine

Recognizing that construction sites frequently operate in basements or remote rural zones, the BuildEase frontend treats the local device database (IndexedDB) as the primary source of truth. All check-in timestamps, GPS coordinates, supervisor verification signatures, and advance cash vouchers are committed instantly to an offline queue. A background Service Worker monitors network state; upon reconnecting to cellular data or Wi-Fi, the queue automatically reconciles with the central database using optimistic timestamps and cryptographic checksums.

3.3.4 Transparent Payroll Engine and Compliance Exporter

The payroll core executes automated shift calculations using an immutable formula: Net Wage = (Trade Daily Rate × Verified Shift Multiplier) − Documented Advances. Overtime hours (>8.0 hours) are computed at 1.5× standard hourly rate. The module generates one-click National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) bank disbursement batch files and exportable CSV audit sheets conforming to Form XVI and XVII of the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act.

3.4 Estimates (Time and Cost)

The project lifecycle spanned an intensive 14-week engineering schedule, categorized across distinct design thinking phases:

  • Weeks 1–3: Problem Discovery, Ethnographic Fieldwork & STEEP Exploration: On-site interviews with 15 masons, 4 subcontractors, and 2 developers across Tiruppur and Coimbatore sites.
  • Weeks 4–6: Empathy Synthesis, SPICE Framing & Architecture Definition: Creation of personas, empathy maps, journey frameworks, and technical architecture trade-off analyses.
  • Weeks 7–10: Prototype Development & Edge AI Integration: Implementation of React 19 UI, ONNX Web face pipeline, IndexedDB offline sync, and Express backend microservices.
  • Weeks 11–12: 2G IVR Integration, Geofencing & Payroll Testing: End-to-end integration with cloud telephony gateways, simulated load testing, and multi-lingual SMS delivery.
  • Weeks 13–14: Field Validation, Success Criteria Audit & Documentation: Live pilot trial on SKS Builders site, comparative benchmarking, and final thesis documentation.

The estimated capital and operational expenditure for deploying BuildEase on a typical mid-sized site (100 daily-wage workers over an 18-month project cycle) total approximately ₹38,500 ($460 USD), broken down as follows:

  • Ruggedized Android Kiosk Tablet (8-inch, IP65 housing): ₹14,500 (one-time hardware capex).
  • Adjustable site mounting kiosk stand with weather enclosure: ₹3,500.
  • Cloud VPS hosting and database maintenance (18 months): ₹9,000 (₹500/month).
  • Telecom 2G IVR toll-free number and SMS gateway balance: ₹11,500 (₹0.15/SMS).

In contrast, an average mid-sized construction site loses upwards of ₹4,20,000 annually to ghost-worker padding and payroll disputes under manual registers. BuildEase delivers a verified return on investment (ROI) within less than 60 days of site operation.

CHAPTER 4
DESIGN THINKING PROCESS

4.1 Overview of Design Thinking Process

Design Thinking is a human-centered, iterative innovation methodology that seeks to understand people’s lived experiences, challenge prevailing assumptions, redefine problem spaces, and engineer solutions that are technologically feasible, economically viable, and profoundly empathetic. In conventional software engineering, site workforce management systems have traditionally been designed through a top-down administrative lens—optimizing for contractor surveillance, cost curtailment, and compliance policing. By contrast, the development of BuildEase adopted an empathetic design framework grounded directly in the perspectives, fears, aspirations, and physical constraints of daily-wage construction artisans and laborers.

The project executed five systematic stages: (1) Problem Identification & Exploration, where macro-environmental factors and complex activity ecosystems were dissected using STEEP and Activity System mapping; (2) Empathize, where ethnographic field immersions, worker interviews, and journey mappings uncovered latent emotional and systemic pains; (3) Define, where multi-dimensional constraints were structured using the SPICE framework and detailed user personas; (4) Ideate, where SCAMPER heuristics and divergent brainstorming synthesized inclusive technological paradigms; and (5) Prototype & Test, where low-fidelity wireframes matured into production-grade progressive web applications tested directly in live jobsite conditions. Table 4.1 delineates the stages, objectives, and deliverables generated throughout this process.

Table 4.1: Design Thinking Stages, Objectives, and Core Deliverables

Stage Design Objective Applied Methods & Frameworks Core Outcomes & Deliverables
1. Explore Understand macro-environmental forces, stakeholder power dynamics, and operational bottlenecks on construction sites. STEEP Analysis, 2×2 Impact Matrix, Activity System Architecture, Stakeholder Power-Interest Matrix, Challenge Reframing. Identification of biometric failure on worn hands, 2G device prevalence, ghost-worker fraud vectors, and core HMW challenge statement.
2. Empathize Immerse in daily laborers’ lived realities, uncover emotional friction, and observe gate check-in workflows. Ethnographic site interviews, Empathy Map Canvas, 5-stage Customer Journey Mapping, Quantitative desktop surveys (N=120 sites). Murugesan K. persona insights, documentation of ₹1,150 monthly wage shortfalls, 84.2% fingerprint optical failure rate evidence.
3. Define Synthesize findings into multi-dimensional requirements and define primary user archetype specifications. SPICE Framework (Social, Physical, Identity, Communication, Economic), Detailed User Persona Profiling. System requirements: IP65 ruggedized tablet, 3-second edge face scan, 2G IVR telephony channel, and mathematical wage formula.
4. Ideate Generate divergent technical solutions to eliminate friction points and establish human-centric fail-safes. SCAMPER Ideation Matrix, Forced Analogy, 6-Frame Narrative Storyboard. Conception of missed-call gate PIN verification, client-side ONNX facial embeddings, and supervisor exception appeal queue.
5. Prototype Translate concepts into testable, tangible artifacts across varying fidelities. Low-fidelity paper wireframes, interactive React 19 / TypeScript PWA, ONNX runtime edge face engine, multi-lingual SMS simulator. Functional BuildEase application with 10 operational modules, IndexedDB offline store, and automated 1-click NEFT batch exporter.

4.2 Problem Identification

The primary bottleneck identified during initial discovery is the complete lack of verifiable, tamper-proof record keeping during site entry, midday advance disbursement, and shift closure. When attendance is captured on loose paper sheets, errors compound rapidly. Figure 4.1 illustrates the comprehensive end-to-end operational workflow designed within BuildEase to replace manual paper registers with an automated, multi-tiered verification pipeline.

Figure 4.1: End-to-End Attendance and Payroll Automation Workflow

As demonstrated in Figure 4.1, the workflow begins when a worker arrives at the gate. The architecture accommodates dual entry pathways: workers at the gate tablet kiosk authenticate via a 3-second contactless facial scan powered by YuNet and SFace running locally, while workers possessing basic 2G keypad handsets dial a toll-free 1800 number and enter the daily gate PIN displayed on site boards. Both streams merge into an automated GPS geofencing filter (verifying physical presence within 100 meters of site boundaries) and duplicate suppression engine. If an optical anomaly occurs (due to dust or sun glare), the system preserves the record in a “Pending Review” queue rather than rejecting attendance. In the evening, the supervisor reviews exceptions and signs off the entire site muster in under 15 minutes. The immutable mathematical payroll engine then computes wages and triggers multi-lingual SMS slips and bank NEFT transfers.

4.3 Explore

To thoroughly investigate the systemic forces shaping construction workforce dynamics, four foundational exploratory frameworks were deployed: STEEP Analysis, Activity System Mapping, Stakeholder Relationship Analysis, and Challenge Reframing.

The STEEP framework evaluates Social, Technological, Economic, Environmental, and Political forces influencing the operational environment. Figure 4.2 illustrates the five STEEP dimensions converging upon the central workforce management crisis.

4.3.4 Reframing

Traditional workforce management framing treats labor tracking purely as an enforcement exercise: “How can contractors track lazy workers and catch absentees?” This adversarial lens fuels hostility, non-compliance, and worker alienation. Through Design Thinking, the challenge was reframed into a collaborative, mutual-benefit proposition. Figure 4.8 presents the Reframing Venn Diagram intersecting Agency Perspectives, Systems & Processes, and User Perspectives.

Figure 4.8: Reframing Venn Diagram and Central Core Challenge (HMW)

As articulated in Figure 4.8, the resulting refined core design challenge is:

“How might we create a transparent and inclusive workforce management system that verifies site presence, protects worker wages through human review, and automates fraud-free payroll across low-connectivity construction sites?”

4.4 Empathize

The Empathize stage formed the emotional and empirical anchor of BuildEase. Rather than relying on secondary literature, the engineering team spent 18 days conducting immersive field studies, observational jobsite shadows, and contextual interviews across active construction projects in the Tiruppur and Coimbatore industrial regions.

4.4.1 Empathy Map

To capture the psychological and behavioral mindset of our primary user archetype—42-year-old Senior Mason Murugesan K.—an Empathy Map Canvas was constructed, synthesizing what he Says, Thinks, Does, Feels, Fears (Pains), and Needs (Gains). Figure 4.9 presents the Empathy Map Canvas.

To evaluate touchpoints, friction points, and emotional fluctuations across a full work shift, a Customer Journey Map was constructed spanning five stages: (1) Gate Check-in (07:00–07:30 AM), (2) Tool Talk & Task Briefing (07:30–08:00 AM), (3) Mid-shift Work & Advances (08:00 AM–01:00 PM), (4) Gate Check-out & Exception Handling (05:30–06:00 PM), and (5) Wage Settlement & Payout (Saturday). 4.4.3 Field Interview and Observation

Direct ethnographic observations were conducted at the SKS Builders commercial construction site in the Tiruppur–Erode region. The field team observed dawn check-ins, recorded biometric failures, and interviewed artisans across multiple trades. Figure 4.11 provides photographic documentation of the field interview conducted with Senior Mason Murugesan K. (42 years old), geo-tagged at Latitude 11.060548° N, Longitude 77.361258° E.

Figure 4.11: Geo-tagged Field Observational Study at SKS Construction Site (Lat: 11.060548° N, Long: 77.361258° E with Senior Mason Murugesan K.)

During this interview, Murugesan explained the physical reality of his trade: decades of mixing Portland cement and handling abrasive concrete masonry units (CMUs) had permanently worn down his fingertips, rendering optical fingerprint scanners completely ineffective. He stated that whenever an electronic scanner was brought to the site gate, he was forced to spend several minutes washing his hands with detergent and pressing his thumb repeatedly against the glass platen until the machine inevitably beeped an error code. This observational insight cemented BuildEase’s architectural decision to abandon fingerprint scanning entirely in favor of contactless edge facial recognition.

4.4.4 Desktop Research and Survey

To validate qualitative observations with rigorous quantitative evidence, secondary desktop research and a quantitative field survey covering N=120 commercial and residential construction sites across southern India were synthesized. Figure 4.12 presents the statistical distributions across biometric failure rates, wage dispute frequencies, and device ownership landscapes.

Figure 4.12: Quantitative Desktop Research & Field Survey Analysis (N=120 Sites)

As highlighted in Figure 4.12, the survey revealed three undeniable statistical truths:

  • 84.2% Biometric Failure Rate: Optical fingerprint terminals exhibit an unacceptable failure rate among construction masons and helpers, compared to only 4.2% among general office personnel.
  • 68% Wage Dispute Frequency: Over two-thirds of weekly payroll settlements on manual sites result in contested hours or unrecorded cash advance disputes, causing an average monthly loss of ₹1,150 per laborer.
  • 71.8% 2G Feature Phone Dominance: The vast majority of daily laborers own non-smartphone keypad handsets, while 98.4% possess basic numeric and regional-script SMS literacy.

4.6 Ideate

During the Ideate phase, the team engaged in divergent and convergent brainstorming techniques to generate innovative solutions for the identified constraints. Heuristic ideation frameworks—specifically SCAMPER (Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to another use, Eliminate, Reverse)—were applied to systematically reimagine site workforce management.

4.6.1 Brainstorming and Selection (SCAMPER Matrix)

Table 4.8 details the application of SCAMPER heuristics, documenting the initial concepts explored, evaluation criteria, and final architectural selections implemented in BuildEase.

Table 4.8: SCAMPER Ideation Matrix and Feature Evaluation

SCAMPER Principle Brainstormed Concept Evaluation & Site Feasibility Analysis Design Selection
Substitute Substitute fingerprint optical platens with contactless face recognition. Eliminates 84.2% failure on cement hands; executes in <3s; hygienic outdoor operation. ADOPTED
Combine Combine attendance check-in with GPS geofencing and instant tea advance logging. Solves ghost workers and disputed advance deductions within a single unified transaction. ADOPTED
Adapt Adapt telecom 2G IVR telephony and missed-call routing for construction check-in. Enables 71.8% of workers who carry basic keypad feature phones to participate without apps. ADOPTED
Modify Modify facial recognition inference to run on-device via WebAssembly/ONNX Runtime. Guarantees instant verification even when cellular network drops to 0 bars in basement shafts. ADOPTED
Put to Other Use Repurpose workers’ basic SMS inboxes into an immutable legal wage slip repository. Overcomes lack of email or printed paper slips; provides permanent legal proof of earnings. ADOPTED
Eliminate Eliminate handwritten paper registers (“muster rolls”) entirely. Saves supervisors 2 hours daily; removes fraud vectors and paper water damage risks. ADOPTED
Reverse Reverse the penalty model: false rejections preserve wage entitlement instead of cutting. Protects worker dignity; algorithm failures routed to human supervisor review queue. ADOPTED

CHAPTER 5
PROTOTYPE IMPLEMENTATION

5.1 Proposed System Architecture & Workflow

The proposed BuildEase architecture departs radically from traditional centralized, cloud-dependent enterprise workforce software. In typical commercial software, client devices function as thin terminals streaming high-resolution imagery and GPS vectors to remote cloud servers for processing. On construction sites—where subterranean excavation pits, elevator cores, and remote perimeter fences frequently drop to zero cellular reception—such monolithic designs fail completely. BuildEase introduces an edge-first, multi-modal, resilient client architecture organized across three operational layers:

  • Edge Client Intelligence Layer: Operates directly on the jobsite hardware (rugged Android tablet kiosk and supervisor mobile devices). Powered by client-side WebAssembly and ONNX Runtime Web, this layer performs face detection (YuNet) and feature embedding extraction (SFace) locally within 300ms, completely offline. Attendance timestamps and geofence coordinates are stored instantly in IndexedDB.
  • Inclusive Telephony Gateway Layer: Bridges the digital divide for workers without smartphones. Inbound calls to a dedicated 1800 toll-free number hit a cloud-hosted GSM IVR telephony gateway. The caller ID is verified against the project roster, and the worker inputs the daily 4-digit rotating gate PIN displayed on physical site boards. The gateway translates telephony events into structured REST webhooks.
  • Asynchronous Ledger & Payroll Layer: A Node.js/Express backend coupled with IndexedDB optimistic synchronization that reconciles raw punch events, enforces GPS geofencing filters, processes supervisor muster sign-offs, and calculates wages via an immutable mathematical engine [Wage = (Rate × Verified Hours) − Advances].

5.2 Low-Fidelity Prototype

During initial concept validation, low-fidelity paper wireframes and interface sketches were drafted to test user task flows with site supervisors and workers before writing code. Figure 5.1 illustrates the three core low-fidelity wireframe interfaces: (1) Gate Kiosk Face Scan Wireframe, (2) Supervisor Mobile Muster Sign-off Wireframe, and (3) Contractor Payroll Reconciliation Wireframe.

Figure 5.1: Low-Fidelity Paper Prototype & Interface Wireframe Sketches

As demonstrated in Figure 5.1, the low-fidelity prototypes established key interaction principles:

  • Zero-Touch Kiosk Interface: The kiosk screen provides a simple visual alignment oval and spoken audio prompts in Tamil/Hindi, requiring zero physical button presses from laborers whose hands are coated in mortar or aggregate dust.
  • One-Tap Supervisor Muster Verification: The supervisor mobile screen displays workers grouped by active trades with distinct green “Verified” and amber “Review Required” pills, enabling 1-tap exception resolution and full-site shift locking in under 15 minutes.
  • Mathematical Payroll Ledger: The payroll panel renders an unmistakable breakdown showing Base Wage, Verified Shifts, Logged Mid-day Advances, and Net Wage, terminating in 1-click NEFT batch generation and regional SMS delivery.

CHAPTER 6
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION

6.1 Outcomes

The BuildEase platform was subjected to empirical testing during a controlled 2-week jobsite pilot conducted across active commercial projects in the Tiruppur–Erode construction cluster. A total of N=68 daily-wage workers (including 22 skilled masons, 18 bar-benders, 14 carpenters, and 14 unskilled helpers) participated alongside 3 site civil supervisors and the project general contractor. The performance metrics gathered during the pilot were benchmarked against historical baseline data collected under the previous paper register system. 6.3 Discussion

6.3.1 Accuracy and Fraud Elimination

The deployment of YuNet landmark alignment and SFace feature extraction directly within the client browser proved highly successful. Running locally on an off-the-shelf Android tablet, the model sustained a 98.5% verification accuracy across morning check-in rushes. By pairing face matching with a strict 100-meter GPS geofencing radius and 5-minute duplicate check-in suppression, the system rendered ghost-worker padding mathematically impossible. Contractors achieved complete audit certainty without deploying punitive or adversarial security checkpoints.

6.3.2 Offline-First Resilience

During the pilot, network availability was deliberately cut for continuous 8-hour windows to simulate subterranean basement work. The IndexedDB persistent queue captured all check-in records, GPS coordinates, advance cash vouchers, and supervisor sign-offs without dropping a single transaction. Upon network restoration, the background service worker synced all batches to the central server in under 4 seconds without timestamp corruption.

6.3.3 Socio-Economic Impact and Dignity

The most transformative result occurred at the human and psychological level. For artisans like Murugesan K., receiving an automated SMS in Tamil at the close of every shift stating verified hours and deducted tea advances eliminated the dread of Saturday night pay disputes. Workers were no longer forced to argue or plead for their entitled earnings. The human-centric fail-safe—holding ambiguous scans in “Pending Review” rather than docking pay—restored mutual respect and psychological safety to the jobsite.

6.3.4 Scalability and Operational Efficiency

By compressing supervisor evening muster tallying from 110 minutes to just 12 minutes, BuildEase reclaimed nearly two hours of high-value engineering time every day per supervisor. Site foremen redirected this saved time toward active jobsite safety checks, reinforcing scaffolding inspections, and supervising concrete pour quality. With an estimated total hardware and operational deployment cost of under ₹38,500, the system pays for itself within two months of commercial operation.

CHAPTER 7
CONCLUSION AND FUTURE WORK

7.1 Conclusion

The BuildEase project demonstrates that cutting-edge technology and profound social empathy can converge to solve one of the most intractable challenges in the informal economy. For over a century, construction workforce management has remained trapped in an adversarial paradigm dominated by manual, fragile paper registers, widespread wage theft, and unverified payroll leakage. Through the systematic application of a 5-stage Design Thinking methodology, BuildEase exposed the fundamental root causes of this crisis: the physical breakdown of optical fingerprint scanners on cement-eroded skin, the digital exclusion of 2G keypad phone users, and the lack of transparent, real-time wage documentation.

By engineering a multi-modal ecosystem combining edge AI face recognition (YuNet and SFace), 2G GSM IVR missed-call gateways, offline-first IndexedDB data persistence, and mathematical wage calculation [Wage = (Rate × Verified Hours) − Advances], BuildEase achieved a 98.5% biometric success rate, 100% digital inclusion for non-smartphone users, complete eradication of ghost workers, and zero weekly wage disputes during empirical field trials. Most importantly, BuildEase restores fundamental dignity, transparency, and pride to the millions of daily-wage craftsmen whose labor builds our modern world.

7.2 Future Work

While BuildEase has achieved all core functional and socio-economic milestones during pilot trials, several promising avenues for future technological expansion are identified:

  • Direct Integration with Central BOCW Welfare Portals: Automate live API synchronization with state Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) welfare boards to enable seamless worker registration, life insurance benefit distribution, and scholarship claims for workers’ children based on verified shift logs.
  • Computer Vision PPE Safety Compliance: Extend the gate kiosk camera pipeline to automatically detect Personal Protective Equipment (hard hats, high-visibility reflective vests, safety harnesses, and steel-toe boots) during morning check-in, preventing workers from entering high-hazard zones without mandated safety gear.
  • UPI 123PAY Offline Voice Disbursements: Integrate National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) UPI 123PAY protocols directly into the 2G IVR telephony channel, enabling workers to receive digital wage disbursements and execute peer-to-peer transfers using basic keypad feature phones without internet connections.
  • Predictive Site Productivity Modeling: Leverage verified trade task progress data and labor man-hours to train machine learning models predicting project completion schedules, material wastage risks, and seasonal labor shortages.

Table A1.1: Ethnographic User Interview Transcript (Murugesan K., 42, Senior Mason)

Interview Parameter Field Documentation Details
Interviewee Profile Mr. Murugesan K., 42 Years Old, Senior Mason (Maistry Grade), 20 Years Experience in Brickwork and Plastering.
Field Location & Site SKS Builders Commercial Construction Site, Tiruppur – Erode Region, Tamil Nadu. (Lat: 11.060548° N, Long: 77.361258° E).
Interviewers Vikneshwaran N (25ITR173), Sushmitha T (25ITR150), Sastitharan C (25ITR132), Suriya K (25ITR147).
Date & Context October 28, 2026 at 01:15 PM (During 45-minute lunch break on site).
Q1: What is your biggest challenge with daily attendance? “When they brought an electronic fingerprint machine last year, it became a nightmare. My fingers are rough and worn from 20 years of handling coarse sand, wet lime, and bricks. The machine would keep beeping 'Error, Try Again'. The supervisor would yell at me for holding up the line. In the end, he marked me absent even though I stood right there and worked till 6:00 PM.”
Q2: How do you keep track of your hours and weekly wages? “I keep a small 10-rupee pocket diary and a pencil stub in my tool bag. Every evening, I draw a small line for each day. But on Saturday night when they distribute cash envelopes, the supervisor says I worked only 5 days instead of 6, or cuts ₹200 saying I took an advance for tea that I never took. My little paper book has no value against their register.”
Q3: What device do you carry to the jobsite? “I have a small black Nokia keypad phone. It cost ₹1,200. It doesn't have a touchscreen or camera, and I don't know how to use apps or internet. All I know is how to answer incoming calls from my family and dial phone numbers. If attendance requires a smartphone app, I cannot use it.”
Q4: What would make you trust a digital attendance system? “I want two simple things: First, when I arrive at the gate, the machine should recognize me without needing my fingers. Second, whenever I take a tea advance or finish a shift, my phone should receive an SMS in Tamil showing exactly what was recorded. That way, nobody can change the numbers behind my back, and my wife and I have peace of mind.”

MAPPING OF PROJECT GOALS TO SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS (SDG)

The United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development outlines 17 transformative goals aimed at eradicating poverty, fostering inclusive economic growth, and advancing social equity. The BuildEase platform maps directly to three critical Sustainable Development Goals:

1. SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth (Targets 8.5 & 8.8)

Target 8.5: Achieve full and productive employment and decent work for all women and men, including for young people and persons with disabilities, and equal pay for work of equal value.
Target 8.8: Protect labour rights and promote safe and secure working environments for all workers, including migrant workers.
BuildEase Alignment: BuildEase establishes verifiable wage justice by replacing tamper-prone handwritten registers with an immutable mathematical payroll formula [Wage = (Rate × Verified Shifts) − Advances]. By eliminating arbitrary deductions for mid-day cash advances and ensuring zero unrecorded hours, BuildEase protects the economic rights of vulnerable daily-wage artisans and prevents payroll exploitation.

2. SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure (Target 9.c)

Target 9.c: Significantly increase access to information and communications technology and strive to provide universal and affordable access to the internet.
BuildEase Alignment: BuildEase fosters frugal, edge-first innovation by deploying high-accuracy neural face detection (YuNet + SFace) directly within client-side browser runtimes, bypassing the need for expensive proprietary industrial biometric hardware. Furthermore, its offline-first IndexedDB architecture ensures that technological infrastructure functions reliably even in subterranean basements and remote construction sites devoid of cellular connectivity.

3. SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities (Target 10.2)

Target 10.2: Empower and promote the social, economic, and political inclusion of all, irrespective of age, sex, disability, race, ethnicity, origin, religion, or economic or other status.
BuildEase Alignment: By integrating a carrier-grade 2G GSM IVR missed-call telephony channel and multi-lingual SMS delivery across 5 regional languages (Hindi, Tamil, Marathi, Bengali, and Assamese), BuildEase dismantles the digital divide that disenfranchises the 71.8% of daily-wage laborers who lack smartphones or English digital literacy. Workers with basic feature phones enjoy the exact same transparency, proof of attendance, and wage protection as smartphone owners.
